minutes.headline: Parks Commission asked for grant-writing help for Marshall Park and OK'd a Little Free Library; fee change deferred.
minutes.summary: The commission heard park account reports, beach staffing and Recreation updates, vendor fair planning, and a long discussion of Marshall Park user fees. It voted to allow a Little Free Library at Wallace Park, to request professional grant help from the town manager, and to approve October minutes. No fee change was made; a February workshop was planned.

public_comment.topic: Heather (surname heard as Casey/Munkacsy) presented a Little Free Library for Wallace Park at no cost to the town.
A member of the audience asked what the governing goal of raising field fees is and how success would be measured.
Dave said the grant-writing line item sits in General Government under the town manager, and urged hiring a professional grant writer.

votes.motion: Allow Heather to install a Little Free Library at Wallace Park, working with Chris Ruth on installation.
Formally request that the town manager provide professional assistance to reapply for the park grant, Land and Water Conservation Fund grant, ADA grant and other appropriate grants for Marshall Park.

budget_items.what_was_said: Activity so far is mostly Rec programs plus some Veterans Park work; beach, field and program fees come in.
Mostly spent on landscaping; very tight for repairs, hope for more next year.
Finance director wants a budget for the revolving fund; article was a not-to-exceed amount, and salary lines may need increasing.
Bouncy house and dunk tank estimated roughly at a stated cost.
Discussed registration counts and per-player fees paid to the town by baseball and the Phillies.

budget_items.topic: ARPA funds for Marshall Park design
budget_items.what_was_said: Selectmen let the commission keep ARPA funds to finish design of phases one to three.
Town meeting appropriated money for grant writing services; dispute over whether select board or town manager controls it.
A neighboring league reportedly pays field rental per year.

not_audible: Vote outcomes and counts for the grant request, minutes and adjournment were not captured, only that a second was heard.
Several figures about field fees and registrations are garbled.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to let a resident install a Little Free Library at Wallace Park at no cost to the town.
The commission moved to ask the town manager for professional help reapplying for Marshall Park grants; the minutes record the outcome of that vote as not audible.
No change was made to Marshall Park user fees; the commission planned a February workshop on them after a long discussion.
The commission was told the Selectmen let it keep ARPA funds to finish design of the first three phases of Marshall Park.
Staff were asked to return with a lifeguard pay-differential proposal, and a beach staffing and hours analysis was targeted for February.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park fees are undecided, so what local leagues and residents pay to use the fields may change after the February workshop, which is the point to weigh in.
Who controls the money Town Meeting appropriated for grant writing was disputed, and that bears on whether outside grants for Marshall Park get pursued.
Beach staffing and lifeguard pay will come back as proposals, which touches next summer's beach hours and the cost of running them.
watch_next: Parks Commission regular meeting January 15, then a proposed Marshall Park fee workshop February 5; the regular February meeting stays the 19th.
Lifeguard pay-differential proposal and the beach staffing and hours analysis, both due back by February.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the Little Free Library vote, the $50,000 grant writing line, the $700 vendor fair cost, the operating-to-revolving transfer, and the meeting dates. They differ most on the Marshall Park grant vote, which the official minutes show as passed 4-0 while we could not hear the outcome, and on the ARPA figure, where ours reads $2,250 and theirs $225,000. Our attendee list also has misheard names and is missing a member.
